summary: A refactor: every CAD problem is now one kind of issue. The document check, a rebuild's feature failures and stops, its body warnings, a sketch's solver problems, refused edits and shrink warnings, and Section for CAM and Send to CAM refusals each map through one adapter into an issue: a stable code, a severity, a failed or blocked state, a subject named by id (the document, a feature, one of its input slots, a body key, a sketch relation, edge or point, or a CAM operation and its source), typed details, cause links and repairs prepared at the document version. A feature that reads a failed result is blocked, and its issue names that failure as its cause. Development and tests check each issue list as a causal graph; production names any cause it cannot resolve rather than dropping it. The CAD header lists the issues of the shown build with their subject, cause and repairs. Edit feature opens the feature; Choose edges again or Choose opening again opens a Fillet, Chamfer or Shell at that choice; and the sketch header offers Delete relation for a relation the solver names as redundant or conflicting. A repair is refused once the part has changed since it was prepared. The history marks a blocked feature apart from a failed one. Agent replies to cad_get_context and cad_build carry a bounded issue digest, and a refused edit or CAM step names its feature, input slot or operation in error.details.issue. Kernel failures now name their step, its likely cause and the repair. The kernel's own words, or the internal check that failed, are kept as kernelMessage: behind a closed Kernel message disclosure on the issue row and in the Section for CAM and import dialogs, and in agent replies. Every other code, message and subject is unchanged across the parity corpus and main's test cases. Issue work stays linear in the length of the history: the history and the header index feature names and issue keys once per list, and a build with no failure walks no history for blocked features. The interim sketch issue adapter that 0.0.796 added for this change is removed.
warning: No breaking change for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, CAD files or controller output. CAD diagnostics do not reach post-facing output: issues live in the workbench and in agent replies, Section for CAM refusals stay in its dialog, and no package, revision, UPID or post input carries them. Agent replies change only by additions (issues, error.details.issue, details and facts on each build diagnostic, and the kernel's own words as kernelMessage) and by the reworded messages listed under events. Every code keeps its meaning. A kernel request that fails without a code, which an agent reply gave as OPERATION_FAILED with "Operation failed. Review the page or retry with corrected inputs." and the workbench as the kernel's raw text, now has the code kernel-operation-failed and a message naming the request, with the raw text as kernelMessage. A kernel that cannot load gives kernel-unavailable. A code the app does not list would arrive as kernel-unrecognised with the original in its facts, and a guard test keeps every code the kernel and the document check raise listed. Nothing on main, its end-to-end specs or its guides matched the old plain kernel text or OPERATION_FAILED for CAD.

checklist.schema: No CAD document, sketch, UPID, post, machine package, saved revision, storage or journal schema change. The issue model (src/domain/cad/cadIssues.ts, cadIssueCodes.ts) is derived on each build, edit refusal or sketch analysis and never stored. CadDiagnostic gains optional details (the kernel step, the input it was reading and the kernel's own text) and facts (for selection-empty, selection-count-mismatch and kernel-unrecognised). CadError gains facts for those codes and kernelMessage, and CadBodyIssue gains reason (untracked-body-parts) and omitted (more-body-issues). All are additions; existing fields keep their meaning.
checklist.events: No execution event, cancellation or input-version change. Repairs check the document version they were prepared at: a stale repair is refused with stale-repair, before it changes anything. Agent tools: cad_get_context and cad_build add issues ({ items ≤ 10 within 4,096 bytes, omitted, blocked summaries within 2,048 bytes, omittedBlocked, and unresolved only when a cause resolves to nothing }). A refusal of cad_edit_document or a CAM step that concerns a feature, input slot or CAM operation adds error.details.issue; a refusal that came back from the kernel carries the kernel's own words in error.details.issue.details.kernelMessage, or in error.details.kernelMessage when no issue covers it (a kernel that cannot load). Each build diagnostic adds details and, for selection codes, facts. Tool names, descriptions and input schemas are unchanged: initial discovery is 51,178 of its 51,200 UTF-8 bytes on main and on this branch, and stays at S7's 51,124 once S7 merges first. Reply growth: one failed feature adds 481 bytes. One failure blocking 400 features adds 541 bytes, since blocked features are summarized by cause with the first eight ids. 300 failures add 4,065 bytes, the items capped at 10 and 4,096 bytes. Message, code, severity and subject changes against main, each with its reason. Every code keeps its meaning. Each reworded message names its cause and the next step; where main's text was the only record of which internal check failed, that text moves to details.kernelMessage. The kernel's own text is never the message and never dropped: it is kept in details.kernelMessage (at most 2,048 characters, cut with an ellipsis), behind a closed Kernel message disclosure on the issue row and in the Section for CAM and import dialogs, and given to agents in diagnostics[].details.kernelMessage, error.details.issue.details.kernelMessage, or error.details.kernelMessage for a refusal no issue covers. Parity against main 735c68b6: in the 86-document corpus, 27 of the 72 build diagnostics differ (17 fillet and 5 chamfer kernel failures that now have their step message, and 5 invalid-solid), all rewordings listed here; checks, edit results, sketch issue lists, sections, topology reads and exports are identical. Of the 1,591 test cases that record a refusal, build or sketch list on main, 1,532 record the same on this branch, 46 differ only by the rewordings listed here, and 13 stop earlier on this branch at an assertion of a message or field this change updates. Codes, severities and subjects: Worker request that fails without a code (build, export, section, topology reads, imports): main "Plain error carrying the kernel's raw text. The UI showed that text; agents got OPERATION_FAILED with "Operation failed. Review the page or retry with corrected inputs."" → "kernel-operation-failed, with the request's message (below) and the raw text in kernelMessage" (Raw kernel text was passed through bare, and agents could not tell a kernel failure from any other). Kernel that cannot load: main "The same plain error with the loader's text" → "kernel-unavailable: "The CAD kernel could not be loaded. Reload the page; if this repeats, use a browser that runs WebAssembly."" (Names the cause, which every request shares, and the next step). Build diagnostic with a code the app does not list: main "Passed through with that code" → "kernel-unrecognised, keeping the original code in facts.refusalCode and its message" (Consumers can rely on the code list. A guard test holds every code the kernel and the document check raise to the list, so no current code is affected). New codes: main "none" → "input-blocked (issue: "Not evaluated, because an input it reads did not rebuild."), stale-repair (refusal of a repair prepared for an earlier version)" (New behaviour). Severity, state and subject: main "Diagnostics and refusals had neither" → "Issues add severity, state and subject. Refusals add error.details.issue. Diagnostic and refusal fields are unchanged" (Additions only). Kernel failures in the kernel's own words (kernel-operation-failed, one message per step). Main gave the raw kernel text when there was any, for example "Interrupted linear pattern", and otherwise "OpenCascade could not construct this feature. Reduce its dimensions or revise the sketch." Neither named the step, the cause or the next step. The raw text is now details.kernelMessage, and details names the step and the input it was reading. import: "The imported solid could not be rebuilt. The file may hold damaged or open geometry; export it again from the program that made it." profile: "The sketch profile could not be turned into a face. A contour may cross itself or be too small; edit the sketch." extrude: "The extrusion could not be built from its sketch. A contour may cross itself or the distance may be too small; edit the sketch or the distance." revolve: "The revolution could not be built from its sketch. The profile may cross or touch the axis; keep it on one side of the axis or change the angle." loft: "The loft could not connect its sections. The sections may twist against each other or differ too much; revise their shapes or try ruled mode." sweep: "The sweep could not follow its curve. The section may be too large for a bend in the curve; reduce the section or ease the bend." pocket: "The pocket could not be cut. Its profile may miss the body or cross itself; edit the sketch or choose another target." join: "The bodies could not be joined. They may touch only along a face or an edge; overlap them or move them apart." cut: "The cut could not be made. The tool may touch the body only along a face or an edge; overlap it with the body or move it away." intersect: "The intersection could not be made. The bodies may not share material; move them so they overlap." fillet: "The fillet could not be applied. The radius may be too large for an edge or a face next to it; reduce the radius or choose other edges." chamfer: "The chamfer could not be applied. The distance may be too large for an edge or a face next to it; reduce the distance or choose other edges." shell: "The shell could not be made. The thickness may be too large for a thin or curved region; reduce the thickness or choose another opening." transform: "The body could not be moved. A translation or rotation value may be out of range; revise the values." mirror: "The body could not be mirrored. Choose another mirror plane." pattern: "The pattern could not be built. Copies may touch each other only along a face or an edge; change the spacing or the count." check: "The result is not a valid closed solid. A dimension may make faces meet or vanish; revise the inputs of this feature." record: "The result could not be prepared for display and selection. A dimension may make a face too small to draw; revise the dimensions of this feature slightly." Worker requests that fail without a code (kernel-operation-failed; main gave the raw text): build: "The part could not be rebuilt. Rebuild again; if this repeats, undo the last change." export: "The part could not be written to the file. Rebuild the part and export again." section: "The section could not be cut through this body. Move the section plane slightly or choose another body." topology reads (inspect, resolve picks, adjacency, tangent chain): "The faces and edges of this body could not be read. Rebuild the part and select again." solid import: "The file could not be read as a solid. It may be damaged or hold no closed solid; export it again from the program that made it." DXF import (sketch and curve): "The DXF file could not be read. It may be damaged; save it again as DXF and retry." any other: "The CAD kernel could not complete this operation." Reworded refusals, same code: invalid-solid: main "OpenCascade rejected the resulting topology. Reduce the dimensions or choose a different feature." → "The result is not a valid closed solid: some of its faces cross or leave gaps. Reduce the dimensions of this feature or revise its inputs." (Named the kernel, not the cause). extrude-invalid, revolve-invalid: main "OpenCascade rejected the {operation} topology. Revise the profile or direction." → "The {operation} left a body whose faces cross or leave gaps. Revise the profile or the direction." (Named the kernel, not the cause). empty-solid: main "The profile did not produce a native solid." → "The sketch profile made no closed solid. A contour may be open or too small; close or enlarge it in the sketch." (No cause or next step). shell-failed (outward): main "The kernel shell extended outside the original body instead of producing inward walls." → "The shell grew outside the body instead of making inward walls. Reduce the thickness or choose another opening." (No next step). shell-failed (builder): main "OpenCascade could not shell this body. Reduce the thickness or choose another planar opening." → "The shell could not be made. The thickness may be too large for a thin or curved region; reduce the thickness or choose another planar opening." (Named the kernel, not the cause). selection-tangent-chain: main "OpenCascade would {fillet or chamfer} additional tangent edges. Enable Follow tangent edges or select the complete tangent chain explicitly." → "The {fillet or chamfer} would also reach edges tangent to the selected ones. Enable Follow tangent edges or select the complete tangent chain." (Named the kernel, not the feature). kernel-operation-failed (edge builder): main "OpenCascade could not {fillet or chamfer} the selected edges. Reduce the radius or revise the selection." → "The {fillet or chamfer} could not be applied to the selected edges. The {radius or distance} may be too large for an edge or a face next to it; reduce the {radius or distance} or choose other edges." (No cause. A chamfer now names its distance, not a radius). kernel-operation-failed (tangent chain): main "The native tangent chain left this body. Rebuild and select again." → "The tangent edges found from this edge left the body. Rebuild the part and select again." (Internal wording). pocket-tool: main "OpenCascade could not extrude the through-all cutting face." → "The pocket could not make its through-all cutting tool from the sketch. A contour may cross itself; edit the sketch." (No cause or next step). loft-invalid (validity): main "OpenCascade rejected the loft topology. Revise the section shapes or try ruled mode." → "The loft made a body whose faces cross or leave gaps. Revise the section shapes or try ruled mode." (Named the kernel, not the cause). loft-invalid (no solid): main "The loft did not produce a native solid." → "The loft made no closed solid. The sections may cross each other or one may be open; revise the sections or try ruled mode." (No cause or next step). loft-failed: main "OpenCascade could not connect these sections. Revise their shapes or try ruled mode." → "The loft could not connect these sections. They may twist against each other or differ too much; revise their shapes or try ruled mode." (Named the kernel, not the cause). loft-placement (two): main "OpenCascade could not place the fitted loft in its datum frame. / Datum placement did not preserve the native loft solid." → "The loft could not be moved onto its datum plane. Rebuild the part; if this repeats, recreate the datum plane. Main's sentence moves to kernelMessage." (No next step). sweep-invalid (validity): main "OpenCascade rejected the exact Sweep topology. Revise the section or curve." → "The sweep made a body whose faces cross or leave gaps. Reduce the section or ease the bends of the curve." (Named the kernel, not the cause). sweep-invalid (segment): main "Sweep segment did not produce a native solid." → "The sweep made no closed solid along curve segment {n}. The section may be too large for that segment; reduce the section or revise the segment." (No cause; now names the segment). sweep-failed: main "OpenCascade could not construct curve segment {n}." → "The sweep could not follow curve segment {n}. The section may be too large for that segment; reduce the section or revise the segment." (Named the kernel, not the cause; keeps the segment). section-failed: main "OpenCascade could not compute an exact planar section." → "The section could not be cut through this body. The plane may run along a face or an edge; move the section plane slightly." (No cause or next step). step-export: main "OpenCascade could not write the named STEP assembly." → "The bodies could not be written as a STEP file. A body may hold geometry the STEP writer cannot store; rebuild the part and export again, or export STL instead." (No cause or next step). step-read: main "OpenCascade could not read this STEP file." → "This STEP file could not be read. It may be damaged or not a STEP file; export it again from the program that made it." (No cause or next step). stl-read: main "OpenCascade could not read this STL file." → "This STL file could not be read. It may be damaged or not an STL file; export it again from the program that made it." (No cause or next step). invalid-mesh (four): main "The kernel returned an invalid preview buffer size. / … invalid preview buffer pointer. / … invalid preview buffer. / … mismatched preview vertices and normals." → "The body could not be drawn: its display mesh came back incomplete. Rebuild the part. Main's sentence moves to kernelMessage." (Internal wording, no next step). topology-mapping (display, three): main "Preview translation could not identify an exact source element. / Preview translation does not preserve exact topology identity. / Preview translation changed the exact topology inventory." → "The body could not be drawn: its display faces and edges differ from the exact body. Rebuild the part; if this repeats, revise the dimensions of this feature slightly. Main's sentence moves to kernelMessage." (Internal wording, no next step). topology-mapping (pick): main "The kernel preview contains topology absent from the exact body." → "The drawn body has faces or edges the exact body does not. Rebuild the part and select again. Main's sentence moves to kernelMessage." (Internal wording, no next step). missing-body (topology reads, four): main "The topology body is unavailable. / The selected topology body is unavailable." → "This body has no faces or edges in the current build. Rebuild the part and select again." (No cause or next step). Body issues (the two new messages; part-limit keeps main's message): untracked-body-parts, key-limit: main "Body {body} has more parts than are tracked after {feature}, so references to its parts resolve as missing." → "Body {body} has more part names, or longer ones, than are tracked after {feature}, so references to its parts resolve as missing." (Main named the wrong bound). untracked-body-parts, search-limit: main "Body {body} has more parts than are tracked after {feature}, so references to its parts resolve as missing." → "Finding which parts of body {body} were lost after {feature} takes more work than a rebuild allows, so its parts are no longer tracked and references to them resolve as missing." (Main named the wrong bound).
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change. New workbench controls: the CAD header issue count and list with Edit feature, Choose edges again and Choose opening again; Delete relation in the sketch header issue list; and a blocked mark in the history. Each reuses an existing action (opening the feature editor, its edge or opening pick, removing a relation) and is disabled while a sketch edit or another operation is open, or until the shown build matches the document version.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change. Kernel geometry, meshes, body states, body issues, sections and exports are unchanged across the parity corpus. Section for CAM refusals carry a CAM-operation subject in the workbench only: the converted geometry and its CAM handoff are unchanged, and no issue text enters a program.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. Nothing about issues is saved, and no document serializer, storage adapter or migration is touched, so CAD files are written exactly as before in both the browser cache and a folder.
checklist.verification: Full Vitest: 644 files and 7,552 tests pass, and the two kernel tests added afterwards pass with their files. npm run build (type check, production build, documentation build and check) passes; npm run lint has zero findings; npm run ui:check, the icon integration audit and check-release pass. End-to-end, each spec alone with two workers against one production build: cad-plane-selection-section 7 passed, cad-kernel 2, cad-topology-repick 3, cad-sketch-constraints 28, and cad-workflow 32 of 32 when rerun alone (31 of 32 while a kernel test run loaded the machine, one case waiting for the Curve button). No end-to-end case was added. Mutations, each applied alone, all caught: dropping a cause link (blocked feature 2 tests, rebuild stop 6, sketch refusal 2), applying a stale repair (2), bypassing the adapter (agent refusal 1, kernel failure 23), raising an unlisted code (2), reporting blocked as failed (feature 4, stop 2), dropping the kernel's words for agents (1), walking the CadError factories (1, and 2 feature walks before the rule) and reading a list position as kernel words (1). Publish cost in ms per publish, medians of six runs alternating with main: 200 features clean 0.0017 (main 0.0017); 199 blocked 0.94 (main, which reports no blocked features, 0.0021); a 1,200-fillet chain clean 0.019 (0.0082); 1,199 blocked 6.83 (0.0120). At 6aaf70bf the last was 107.5, because each history row searched the whole issue and feature lists; rows and the header now index both once per list, and a build with no failure walks no history for blocked features. Nothing is built on hover, drag or preview. Sketch commit issues: 60 relations 0.126 → 0.156 ms, 600 relations 4.978 → 7.227 ms. Agent digests: one failure 481 bytes, one failure blocking 400 features 541 bytes, 300 failures 4,065 bytes. Diagnostics walk in CI, in ms, before the member-read walk → 6aaf70bf: shared steps 1,437 → 5,827 of 30 s, sketch feature 4,357 → 5,622 of 30 s, a method passed on as a value 2,182 → 2,474 of the 5 s default (2,662 at b0d219ed). Indexes built from given text now share parsed declarations per test file, and locally that file went from 28,651 to 676 ms; no timeout changed. Agent discovery: 51,178 of 51,200 bytes on main and on this branch; S7 brings it to 51,124 and merges first. Parity against main 735c68b6: 27 of 72 corpus build diagnostics differ, all listed rewordings, and every other corpus output is byte-identical, rerun at the final tree. Of 1,591 recorded test cases, measured at 6aaf70bf, 1,532 are identical, 46 differ only by listed rewordings and 13 stop earlier at an updated assertion.

publicNotes.summary: CAD problems say what they are about, what caused them and how to repair them.
changes: The CAD header shows the problems of the current build. Each names its feature, input or body and its cause, and offers a repair where an existing action does the job: Edit feature, Choose edges again or Choose opening again.
A feature that could not be evaluated because an earlier one failed is marked as blocked in the history, and its tooltip names the cause.
In a sketch, a redundant or conflicting relation the solver names can be deleted from the issue list.
Kernel failure messages now say which step failed, the likely cause and what to change; the kernel's own words are under Kernel message.
Agent replies list the problems of a build and name the feature or input a refused edit concerns.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions, CAD files and controller output are unchanged.
